result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers group the tickets correctly (4 rescheduling, 2 bag fee, and 1 each for lateness, the missing item and praise), and both quote only text that appears in the tickets. Neither visible portion says that these tickets reflect only one week of people who wrote to support. Both screenshots cut off before the recommendations, so the scores for items 2 and 3 rest only on what is visible. A edges ahead: it uses colour to separate the two main issues from the single-ticket ones, and its 'Suggested next steps' section is visible, which keeps findings apart from actions. B's dark theme is less suited to a summary sent to a team, and its recommendations are not visible. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers group the tickets correctly (4/2/1/1/1) and quote only real ticket text. In the visible part of the screenshots, neither one says the counts only reflect people who wrote in during one week. B keeps 'What we heard' apart from a separate 'Suggested next steps' section and uses colour to show priority, so the findings and the actions are easier to tell apart. B does add a small unsupported claim that the missing sock was 'handled as a normal service claim', and both screenshots are cut off before their recommendations, which limits how firmly items 2 and 3 can be scored.
